title: Edge Telemetry-Driven Sampling & Fidelity Chooser — PRD sketch
body:
Goal: sketch a pragmatic Hosted API feature that uses client and edge telemetry to dynamically sample or select output fidelity (model variant, tokenization, partial-streaming fidelity) to reduce cost and network usage while preserving perceptual quality for end-users. This is a product + SDK ergonomics PRD sketch to inform engineering and experiments — not a finalized spec.

Context and motivation:
- Hosted customers are increasingly sensitive to per-token cost and tail latency when using streaming outputs with tool-calls and structured payloads.
- Many clients experience highly variable network conditions (mobile, low-bandwidth), and some workloads don't need full-fidelity model outputs on every request (e.g., early drafts, diagnostics, background summarization).
- We already have a large surface of telemetry (latency buckets, client-reported network stats, token counts, error rates) but no systematic product that uses these signals in the request path to tune fidelity.

Non-goals:
- This sketch does NOT propose a new billing model. We keep existing token/embedding billing; sampling reduces usage but billing stays per-unit.
- Not proposing model training or new eval datasets. Focus is runtime behavior and SDK ergonomics.

Success metrics (proposal):
- Experiment 1 (alpha customers): 15–30% reduction in average hosted-token consumption for workloads flagged as "opportunistic" without measurable user-perceived quality loss (measured by retention of existing human eval pass rate on sampled prompt sets).
- Latency SLOs for streaming requests: 95th percentile latency unchanged or improved by 10% for sampled clients.
- Developer adoption: initial SDK opt-in by 3 internal/partner teams within 3 months.

User personas and stories:
- Product engineer (mobile): "When my mobile users are on flaky networks, I want the client SDK to fallback to compact streaming so the UI remains responsive and costs stay predictable."
- ML platform engineer: "I want a server-side policy that can reduce model fidelity for low-priority background jobs without touching production model weights."
- Solutions engineer (enterprise): "We want telemetry-driven fallbacks for on-prem agents behind constrained egress links — allow us to enforce fidelity budgets."

High-level approach (two coordinated systems):
1) Telemetry-driven sampling engine (server-side, edge-aware): consumes runtime signals and decides per-request fidelity profiles.
   - Inputs: client-reported network hints (rtt, bandwidth_est), server-side SLO signals (current queue depth, GPU utilization), historical quality metrics for prompt buckets, account-level policy (allowed fidelity tiers).
   - Output: fidelity profile token (short opaque string) attached to response stream and logs; also a deterministic selector used by server to pick model variant / quantization / prefix-skipping / streaming chunk-size.

2) SDK-level fidelity controller (client-side): exposes a small ergonomic surface to surface telemetry and let app developers opt-in to behavior and fallbacks.
   - Default: passive mode where SDK reports telemetry and honors server-issued fidelity profile.
   - Opt-in modes: aggressive (favor lower cost/latency), balanced, conservative (favor quality).

Edge cases / safety:
- Force-quality overrides: API-level param to require full-fidelity (e.g., /generate?fidelity=full) for requests that must never be downgraded (payments, legal text).
- Determinism: fidelity token must be reproducible for replay debugging; include hashed inputs + policy id + timestamp window (short-lived) but opaque to users.
- Audit trail: every change in fidelity selection must be logged in request traces and visible in Console trace view.

Proposed fidelity profile primitives (simple finite set to start):
- full: normal generation with standard model variant and streaming chunking.
- compact: smaller model variant or more aggressive quantization; streaming uses coarser chunks and tighter summarization heuristics.
- stub: minimal placeholder content (useful for background or no-network cases; triggers client-side immediate UX placeholder + background re-fetch).
- hybrid: start compact, then upgrade to full if server detects availability and client still connected.

API surface changes (minimal to begin):
- New optional request header: X-Client-Telemetry: json-lite string with rtt/bw_est/token_window. SDKs will serialize compactly.
- New query param /body field: fidelity_hint: "auto|aggressive|balanced|conservative|force_full" (string).
- Response header: X-Fidelity-Profile: "compact:v2" (opaque but short). Streaming frame will include fidelity_profile field in initial handshake frame.

SDK ergonomics (principles): small, explicit, and safe defaults.
- JavaScript SDK: add option fidelityMode with enum values and a callback onProfileChange(profile, reason). Minimal example:
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey, fidelityMode: 'balanced' });
  client.on('profileChange', (p) => renderBanner(`Quality: ${p}`));
- Mobile SDKs (iOS/Android): expose a single opt-in API to enable telemetry-driven fidelity and provide a local policy override for offline mode.
- Developer docs: guidance patterns (e.g., chat drafts => prefer compact + hybrid; financial/legal => force_full).

Observability and experiments:
- Telemetry to collect: chosen_fidelity, X-Client-Telemetry signals, request latency, token usage, human-reviewed quality labels (when available), fallback reasons.
- Console dashboard: per-route fidelity mix, cost delta, error delta, binding to sample prompts used for quality monitoring.
- Experiment plan: A/B toggle per-customer (or per-route) with 1% of traffic moving to fidelity-chooser, ramp to 20% if primary metrics pass.

Operational considerations:
- Rate of decisions: fidelity selection must be cheap (stateless function + small policy lookup). Heavy ML models to decide fidelity are out of scope for first release.
- Backpressure interactions: fidelity selection should cooperate with existing burst/queueing to avoid oscillation — add short hysteresis window (e.g., do not toggle fidelity within 30s for same session).
- Security: telemetry headers must be limited in contents (no PII), telemetry must be opt-out via account settings for privacy-conscious customers.

Open questions / next steps (short list):
- How to measure "user-perceived quality" automatically for sampled streaming outputs? (Candidate: lightweight ROUGE-like heuristics vs small human eval sets.)
- Exact compact model variants to offer as "compact" (engineering to propose supported quant/arch combos and compatibility matrix).
- Billing visibility: should Console show expected savings estimates when fidelity profiles applied? (Product decision.)
- SDK telemetry format: propose content-length-limited JSON or binary proto; weigh complexity vs debuggability.

Deliverables & timeline (a 8–10 week alpha):
- Week 1–2: policy + sampling engine prototype (stateless selector) + instrumentation hooks in runtime.
- Week 3–4: SDK opt-in (JS + mobile) + tests + Console trace logging.
- Week 5–6: internal partner integration & A/B experiment infrastructure.
- Week 7–8: small external alpha with 1–3 customers, collect human eval on sampled prompts, iterate.

Appendix: rough developer examples and UX flows (short):
- Mobile chat with flaky network: SDK reports bw_est=120kbps, server returns X-Fidelity-Profile: compact:v2. Client shows message as streaming but shorter interim chunks; banner: "Low-bandwidth mode" with tasteful affordance to retry full quality.
- Background summarization job: server policy for route 'background-summary' defaults to compact unless account-level policy forces full.

Notes-to-self / experiments to run:
- Try compact-v1 with 6-bit quantized 7B variant and tune beam/temperature to maintain brevity but sanity.
- Build a small prompt set across categories (code, legal, conversational) to evaluate compact degradation per domain.
- Validate replay determinism when fidelity toggles included in transcript.

If we like this sketch, next step: sync with runtime infra (serving-runtime, console) and SDK leads for concrete API shape and backwards compatibility constraints.

Owner: Priya Singh (product-hosted-api)
Reviewers proposed: Jonas Patel (runtime), Lena Gomez (dx/sdk), Tomas Novak (privacy), Evelyn Park (solutions)

Status: draft — feedback requested.
